lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Right, listen up — here's the situation. The boat, as you can see, is small, it's half-rotten, it leaks in several places, and if it tips even slightly to one side, over it goes. And here you all are, arriving together, every single one of you loaded down with luggage. If you board with all that, I guarantee you'll regret it — especially those of you who can't swim.
lines.note: Opening address to the whole crowd. Matter-of-fact, not threatening. Charon is a tradesman explaining liability.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So what do we do to make the crossing go smoothly?

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: I'll tell you: they board naked. All that excess baggage gets left on the shore. The ferry will barely take them even then. And you, Hermes — your job from this point is to not let a single one of them on unless they're stripped bare, exactly as I said. Stand at the gangplank, inspect them, and make sure they board with nothing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good plan. That's what we'll do. [pause] Right — who's first?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Menippus, that's me. Look, Hermes — the satchel and the walking stick can go straight in the lake. Sensibly, I didn't even bring the cloak.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Board, Menippus — finest of men — and take the seat of honour up by the helmsman where you can keep an eye on everyone. [turning] And who is this good-looking one?
lines.note: Genuine warmth toward Menippus, then immediately businesslike.

lines.speaker: Charon
lines.text: Charmolaos of Megara. Very much in demand. His kiss ran to two talents.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Right, then — off with the beauty. The lips with their kisses, the thick hair, the flush on the cheeks, the skin — all of it. Good. Much lighter. Board.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And you — the one in the purple robe and the diadem, the fierce-looking one — who are you?

lines.speaker: Lampicus
lines.text: Lampicus. Tyrant of Gela.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: So why exactly are you arriving with all that, Lampicus?

lines.speaker: Lampicus
lines.text: What do you mean, why? Was a tyrant supposed to come naked, Hermes?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: A tyrant — no. A corpse — absolutely. Take it off.

lines.speaker: Lampicus
lines.text: Fine. There — the wealth is gone.
lines.note: Each concession is reluctant, negotiated one item at a time.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And the pomposity, Lampicus. And the arrogance. They'll weigh the boat down the moment they hit the hull.

lines.speaker: Lampicus
lines.text: Fine, but at least let me keep the diadem and the robe.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: No. Those too.

lines.speaker: Lampicus
lines.text: All right. Is that everything? I've taken everything off, as you can see.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: The cruelty. The stupidity. The insolence. The temper. Those as well.

lines.speaker: Lampicus
lines.text: [pause] There. I'm bare.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Board. — You, the heavy one, the well-upholstered one. Who are you?

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Damasias. The athlete.
lines.note: Good-natured, compliant once the situation is explained.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes — I thought I recognised you. I've seen you in the gymnasiums often enough.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: Right, Hermes — and I'm already naked, so you can let me through.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Naked? My dear fellow, you're wearing about four hundred pounds of muscle. Strip that off too — you'll sink the boat just putting one foot in. And lose those victory wreaths. And the herald's announcements.

lines.speaker: Damasias
lines.text: There — you see? Genuinely naked now. Same weight as any other corpse.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Much better. Light at last. Board. — And you, Craton — put down the fortune. And the softness, the luxury. Don't bring the grave goods, don't bring the ancestral honours. Leave behind the family name, the reputation, any prizes the city awarded you, the inscriptions on your statues. And don't start telling us about the enormous tomb they heaped up for you — all of that adds weight the moment you mention it.

lines.speaker: Craton
lines.text: Not willingly. But I'll throw it away. [sighs] What else am I going to do?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Right. — And you, the one in armour. What's all this? Why are you carrying a trophy?

lines.speaker: General
lines.text: Because I won, Hermes. I was decorated for valour. The city honoured me.
lines.note: Brief, proud. Doesn't see what the problem is.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Leave the trophy on the surface. In Hades there's peace — no use for weapons down there.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: And this solemn-looking figure — the one with the air of great importance, the raised eyebrows, the deep furrowed thoughts, the beard hanging down to here — who is that?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: A philosopher of some kind, Hermes. Or rather: a fraud, stuffed with conjuring tricks. Strip him too — you'll find all sorts of entertaining things hidden under that cloak.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Right — off with the pose, first. Then all the rest. [takes inventory] Good gods — look at the load he's carrying. What imposture — what ignorance and quarrelsomeness and vanity, what insoluble puzzles, what thorny arguments, what labyrinthine theories — and on top of all that, a truly impressive quantity of wasted effort, not a little drivel, a heap of nonsense, hair-splitting — and, by Zeus, actual gold coins — and indulgence, and shamelessness, and rage, and self-pampering, and weakness — don't think I missed those, however carefully you'd packed them away. And get rid of the dishonesty. And the pomposity. And the conviction that you're better than everyone else. Because if you boarded with all of that, what fifty-oared galley could hold you?
lines.note: The inventory is Hermes letting himself go a little — he's been doing this all day and the hypocrisy is genuinely gratifying to expose.

lines.speaker: The Philosopher
lines.text: Very well. I'll put it all down, since you insist.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Oh — and the beard, Hermes. Make him leave the beard. Look at it. Heavy, matted — that's five minas of hair at minimum.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Correct. The beard goes too.

lines.speaker: The Philosopher
lines.text: And who exactly is going to shave it?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Menippus here — he'll take a shipwright's axe and hack it off, using the gangplank as a chopping block.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Actually, Hermes — hand me a saw instead. More satisfying.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: The axe will do. [sound of chopping] There. You actually look like a human being now that you've put down your own stench.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Shall I trim a bit from the eyebrows as well?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Please — he'd arched them halfway up his forehead. No idea what he was reaching for. [to the Philosopher] What's this? You're crying? You're flinching from death? Get on the boat.
lines.note: The turn from comic to contemptuous is instant.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: There's one more thing — the heaviest item. He's got it tucked under his arm.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What is it, Menippus?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Flattery, Hermes. Served him very well in life.

lines.speaker: The Philosopher
lines.text: Well then, Menippus — you can put down your own things too. Your freedom. Your plain speaking. Your cheerfulness. Your self-sufficiency. And that laugh. You're the only one here who's laughing.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Absolutely not — keep all of that, Menippus. It's light, it's easy to carry, and it'll be useful on the voyage.
lines.note: Final word on Menippus. Hermes allows it without hesitation.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Rhetorician — you, put down the enormous torrent of words. The antitheses. The balanced clauses. The periods. The barbarisms. All the other ballast of oratory.

lines.speaker: Rhetorician
lines.text: Done. Putting it down.
lines.note: The quickest capitulation of the scene. He had nothing to say, which is the joke.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Good. Right — cast off the mooring lines. Take up the gangplank. Haul in the anchor. Make sail. Helmsman, take the tiller. Let's go.
lines.note: A brief burst of competence — Hermes in his element.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Why are you all wailing like this, you idiots? — And you especially, Philosopher, the one who just lost the beard.

lines.speaker: The Philosopher
lines.text: Because, Hermes, I believed the soul was immortal.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: He's lying. That's not what's bothering him.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: What is it, then?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: That he'll never again eat expensive dinners. That he'll never again slip out at night with his cloak pulled over his head to do his rounds of the brothels. That he won't spend his mornings swindling young men out of their money on the pretext of wisdom. Those are the things that are bothering him.
lines.note: Delivered as plain reportage. No relish, no cruelty. That's why it lands.

lines.speaker: The Philosopher
lines.text: And you, Menippus? You're not upset about dying?

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: How could I be? Nobody had to call me. I hurried here on my own.
lines.note: The running gag: Menippus arrived voluntarily.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: But — speaking of other things — isn't that shouting I can hear? Like people calling out from somewhere on the surface?

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: Yes, Menippus — from several places at once, actually. Over there, they're all gathered in the assembly, laughing with relief about Lampicus's death — and his wife is being roughed up by the women, and his young children are getting stoned by the other children, quite enthusiastically. Elsewhere, in Sicyon, they're applauding Diophantus the rhetorician delivering a funeral oration over Craton here. And — yes — Damasias's mother is leading the lamentation with a group of women, weeping loudly over her son. As for you, Menippus — nobody is crying. You're lying there alone, in perfect silence.
lines.note: Hermes ticks through the reports efficiently, slightly amused by the Menippus item.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Don't be so sure. Give it a moment — you'll hear the dogs howling most piteously for me, and the ravens beating their wings together, when they all gather to bury me.
lines.note: Entirely satisfied with this. Not at all sad about it.

lines.speaker: Hermes
lines.text: That's the spirit, Menippus. — Right: we've docked. The rest of you — straight ahead, that way, to the court. Charon and I are going back for the next lot.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Safe crossing, Hermes. — Come on then, let's move. What are you all waiting for? You're going to be judged regardless, and by all accounts the sentences are severe — wheels, rocks, vultures. Every life gets examined in full detail.
lines.note: Menippus herding the reluctant dead toward judgment with cheerful authority, as if he's done this before.
